# Building GenAI Applications with AWS: Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This advanced course teaches you how to architect, develop, and deploy generative AI applications on AWS. It bridges the gap between AI/ML concepts and production-ready AWS services, covering the full lifecycle from model selection and integration to scalable deployment and cost optimization.

**Who this is for:**
- Backend engineers transitioning into AI/ML
- AWS solution architects designing GenAI systems
- Full-stack developers building intelligent applications
- DevOps engineers deploying ML workloads at scale

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
Generative AI is reshaping technical hiring. Interviews increasingly ask about LLM integration, prompt engineering, RAG systems, and AWS ML services. Mastery of this path demonstrates you can handle real-world complexity: working with third-party models (OpenAI, Claude, Llama), managing costs, handling concurrency, and building resilient systems. This is especially valued at FAANG companies and AI-focused startups.

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **AWS AI/ML Services Fundamentals** — SageMaker, Bedrock, Lambda, and service selection patterns
- **Large Language Models & Integration** — Using foundation models (GPT, Claude, Llama), prompt engineering, token management
- **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** — Knowledge bases, embeddings, vector stores, semantic search
- **Generative AI Application Architecture** — Multi-tier design, caching strategies, fallback patterns, cost optimization
- **Real-time & Batch Processing** — Streaming inference, asynchronous jobs, batch transformations
- **Security, Compliance & Cost Management** — API key rotation, fine-grained IAM, spending controls, PII handling
- **Monitoring, Logging & Observability** — CloudWatch integration, latency tracking, error analysis for GenAI workflows
- **Advanced Patterns** — Multi-model ensembles, function calling, agent frameworks (LangChain/LlamaIndex on AWS)

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Foundations (Tasks 1–8)**
Build core understanding of AWS ML services and LLM basics.

1. **AWS AI/ML Service Landscape** — Compare Bedrock vs. SageMaker vs. Lambda for GenAI
2. **Setting Up AWS Environment** — IAM roles, VPCs, CloudFormation templates for ML workflows
3. **Introduction to Foundation Models** — Model capabilities, pricing, latency, context windows
4. **Prompt Engineering Basics** — Few-shot learning, chain-of-thought, system prompts
5. **AWS Bedrock Console & SDK** — Hands-on API calls, response handling
6. **Token Economics** — Calculating input/output costs, optimizing token usage
7. **Error Handling & Rate Limiting** — Exponential backoff, quota management
8. **Local Testing Setup** — LocalStack for offline development, mock APIs

### **Phase 2: Core GenAI Patterns (Tasks 9–25)**
Master essential application patterns.

9. **Text Generation Pipelines** — Streaming responses, buffering, token-level monitoring
10. **Embeddings & Vector Databases** — Creating embeddings with Bedrock, storing in OpenSearch/Pinecone
11. **Similarity Search Implementation** — Cosine similarity, FAISS, semantic search on AWS
12. **Basic RAG System** — Query → Embed → Retrieve → Generate workflow
13. **Chat Applications with Memory** — DynamoDB conversation history, context management
14. **Multi-turn Dialogue** — State machines, conversation threading, context windows
15. **Function Calling / Tool Use** — Structured outputs, agent patterns, deterministic responses
16. **Streaming Responses** — Server-Sent Events (SSE), chunked transfer encoding, client-side buffering
17. **Cost Optimization Strategies** — Model selection, batch processing, caching frequent queries
18. **Prompt Templates & Composition** — Jinja2 templates, dynamic prompt building
19. **Handling Long Documents** — Chunking strategies, recursive summarization, hierarchical RAG
20. **Multimodal Integration** — Image understanding, vision-language models on Bedrock
21. **Output Parsing & Validation** — Pydantic, JSON schema enforcement, fallback parsing
22. **Concurrent Request Handling** — AsyncIO, thread pools, managing concurrency limits
23. **Caching Strategies** — Redis for prompt/response caching, reducing latency and cost
24. **Fallback & Graceful Degradation** — Multiple model fallbacks, rule-based fallbacks
25. **Testing GenAI Applications** — Unit testing prompts, integration tests, cost-aware testing

### **Phase 3: Advanced Architectures (Tasks 26–42)**
Build production-grade systems.

26. **SageMaker Integration** — Deploying custom fine-tuned models, inference endpoints
27. **Batch Transform Jobs** — Processing large datasets asynchronously
28. **Real-time Inference Endpoints** — Multi-model endpoints, A/B testing, blue-green deployments
29. **Workflow Orchestration with Step Functions** — Multi-step GenAI pipelines, error recovery
30. **Event-Driven Architecture** — S3 triggers, SNS/SQS for async processing
31. **Building Knowledge Bases** — Bedrock Knowledge Bases, ingestion pipelines, versioning
32. **Advanced RAG: Hybrid Search** — Combining BM25 + semantic search, ranking strategies
33. **Multi-Agent Systems** — Coordinating multiple specialized LLMs, tool delegation
34. **Agentic Workflows** — Planning, execution, observation loops (ReAct pattern)
35. **Context-Aware Personalization** — User embeddings, dynamic prompt customization
36. **Fine-tuning on AWS** — Preparing datasets, fine-tuning workflows, evaluation
37. **Prompt Injection & Defense** — Detecting adversarial inputs, sanitization, guardrails
38. **Latency Optimization** — Profiling, quantization, edge deployment, distillation
39. **Handling Hallucinations** — Grounding techniques, source attribution, confidence scoring
40. **Multi-turn Agent Loops** — Autonomous agents, tool use chains, loop termination
41. **Large-Scale Inference** — Batch processing terabytes, distributed inference, cost modeling
42. **Monitoring & Observability at Scale** — Custom metrics, anomaly detection, performance dashboards

### **Phase 4: Specialized & Production Topics (Tasks 43–54)**
Deployment, compliance, and advanced patterns.

43. **Security & Data Privacy** — Encryption, data masking, PII detection, compliance (HIPAA, GDPR)
44. **API Gateway & Rate Limiting** — Throttling, quota management, usage plans
45. **CI/CD for GenAI** — Automating prompt testing, model updates, rollback strategies
46. **Infrastructure as Code** — CDK, Terraform for GenAI stacks
47. **Cost Governance** — Budget alerts, optimization recommendations, ROI analysis
48. **Disaster Recovery & HA** — Multi-region setup, failover strategies, disaster recovery drills
49. **Logging & Audit Trails** — CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs, audit compliance
50. **Explainability & Trust** — Source attribution, confidence scores, reasoning traces
51. **A/B Testing Frameworks** — Statistical significance, multi-armed bandits for model selection
52. **Custom Guardrails** — Content filtering, output validation, safety scores
53. **Serverless GenAI Stack** — Lambda-based architecture, cold starts, optimization
54. **Open-Source Model Deployment** — Llama 2, Mistral on SageMaker, self-hosted options

### **Phase 5: Capstone & Interview Prep (Tasks 55–62)**
Real-world scenarios and interview readiness.

55. **Case Study: E-commerce Recommendation Engine** — Product search + RAG + personalization
56. **Case Study: Customer Support Chatbot** — Multi-turn, knowledge base, escalation routing
57. **Case Study: Content Generation Platform** — Batch processing, quality scoring, approval workflows
58. **Performance Tuning Deep-Dive** — End-to-end latency analysis, bottleneck identification
59. **Building a Prompt Testing Framework** — Automated evaluation, A/B testing infrastructure
60. **System Design Interview Simulation** — Designing a GPT-like service on AWS (60 min)
61. **Cost Optimization Challenge** — Reduce bill by 40% while maintaining performance
62. **Production Readiness Checklist** — Security, monitoring, disaster recovery, compliance review
